J.8 must independently re-derive and attack the authority vocabulary before B-149O.20J.4-1 can close. Only after a clean J.8 may 149O.20K (HMIC Class-B Verifier Source-Scope Contract Evolution) become eligible -- and 149O.20K must still perform its own fresh HMIC-REQ-052 transitive authority-dependency closure analysis rather than assuming the HMIC source count changes.
summary: Phase 149O.20J.7 -- Class-B writesecurity/chown ACL-Right Reclassification Narrow Repair: repaired the known-safe-vocabulary gap in B-149O.20J.4-1 independently identified by 149O.20J.6. Before editing, independently inspected HBDC-001 (HBDC-REQ-016/017/020, CBD-1/CBD-3), the current 869-line hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py in full, 149O.20J.5's repair diff and 149O.20J.6's verification document as historical record (not unverified oracle), man chmod's ACL MANIPULATION OPTIONS section read directly on this host, and fresh real chmod +a grants confirming canonical token spelling for every currently-known-safe right (none render with the man-page's hyphenated example form). Derived writesecurity's semantic effect ("Write an object's security information (ownership, mode, ACL)") as transitive write-equivalent authority: a holder can edit the ACL to grant itself add_file/write/etc., flip mode bits directly, or alter ownership-related security metadata -- traced to HBDC-REQ-016/017/020's own directory-entry-replacement/rename reasoning, not merely immediate content writes. Derived chown's semantic effect ("Change an object's ownership") similarly: becoming owner confers ordinary owner-mode-bit write authority with no ACL grant needed, distinguishing the ACL right's semantic authority from OS policy restrictions on which transitions are accepted and from this host's same-owner conditions. Explicitly critiqued and avoided repeating 149O.20J.5's flawed same-owner differential (independently reproduced: an owner can already chmod/chown their own object with no ACL grant at all, so granting vs. not granting is not a meaningful differential in a same-owner fixture) -- no second local user account exists on this host and none was created; classification instead rests on man chmod's primary-source definition plus HBDC's fail-closed posture for unproven-safe rights. Implemented the exact narrow diff: moved writesecurity and chown from _MACOS_ACL_KNOWN_SAFE_RIGHTS to _MACOS_ACL_WRITE_CAPABLE_RIGHTS in hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py (single file, single logical change, combined known-rights vocabulary unchanged), with the transitive-authority classification principle documented directly above both constants. Performed a bounded completeness audit of the entire remaining known-safe vocabulary (read, execute, readattr, readextattr, readsecurity, list, search, file_inherit, directory_inherit, limit_inherit, only_inherit): each individually granted via real chmod +a and confirmed read-only or a non-standalone ACE-inheritance-propagation modifier; no other right shares the defect; noted that only_inherit's interaction with the parser is, if anything, over-classified dangerous (a false positive, not a false negative), consistent with HBDC's fail-closed requirement. Wrote a fresh, independent 72-test module (tests/test_phase_149o_20j_7_class_b_writesecurity_chown_acl_right_reclassification_narrow_repair.py; none copied from 149O.20J.6's suite) covering primary-source semantic derivation, the exact vocabulary diff, the complete known-safe-vocabulary audit, writesecurity/chown real-fixture parser + ground-truth detection on files and directories, principal-resolution regression (current/unrelated user, effective/unrelated group, unresolvable principal, deny-only) for both rights, ancestor-chain composition at a grandparent and a deeper great-grandparent level for both rights, a safe full-chain control reaching the filesystem root, Trusted-Git and Protected-Root composition and equivalence for both rights, existing dangerous-right regression (directory and file), J-1/J-2/J-3/B-149O.20J.2-1/symlink/indeterminate-ACL regressions, HMIC 25/5, zero production consumers, the read-only wall, and real-host NON_COMPLIANT. All 72 tests pass, deterministic across three repeated runs, zero repository mutation. One pre-existing J.6 test (test_writesecurity_and_chown_are_currently_classified_known_safe) asserted the live production classification as of J.6; since this phase intentionally changes that classification (as J.6 itself recommended), the assertion was narrowly updated to pin against the historical J.6 commit blob (git show 4c4fd16d:...) rather than the live module -- preserving the historical record as a permanent, commit-pinned fact rather than leaving it broken by an authorized later change, the same precedent as 149O.20J.5 updating 149O.20J.4's own pre-authorized xfail markers once its repair made them pass. All 67 J.6 tests pass after this update. Broader regression (pytest -k 'class_b or hbdc or 149o_20j' -n auto): clean baseline via git stash push -u (no J.7 changes): 11 failed / 725 passed / 5 skipped / 1 pre-existing collection error; with changes restored: 16 failed / 792 passed / 5 skipped / 1 pre-existing collection error -- the 5 additional failures are exactly the expected working-tree-dirty self-checks from historical phases (149O.20D, 149O.20D.1, 149O.20E, 149O.20H, 149O.20C) that trip on any uncommitted src/ change and self-resolved once this phase's changes were committed (confirmed clean git status --short after commit); zero of the 72 new tests failed. fast_green (pytest -m fast_green -n auto, fido2 module ignored -- pre-existing/unrelated): raw run 81 failed / 6761 passed / 5 skipped / 1 pre-existing collection error; clean-deselected citation (exact raw failing node IDs deselected via argv-list subprocess, not shell string interpolation): 0 failed / 6761 passed / 5 skipped / 1 pre-existing collection error; zero of the 81 raw failures in this phase's own test file. Governed lifecycle: closed the stale post-149O.20J.6 idle placeholder task, opened a fresh governed task 20260812-2330-phase-149o-20j-7-... with the production file, both test files, and this phase's own document allowed, the other two Class-B modules and HMIC-adjacent modules explicitly forbidden. Committed via pcae commit implementation (commit 26545b90) -- staged-file-aware, explicit --path per file (9 files), no raw git commit, no --no-verify, no force push. Wrote docs/PHASE_149O_20J_7_CLASS_B_WRITESECURITY_CHOWN_ACL_RIGHT_RECLASSIFICATION_NARROW_REPAIR.md documenting all required verification areas. Updated PROJECT_STATUS.md (demoting 149O.20J.6 to a new stacked Previous Phase entry) and CHANGELOG.md.
